pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/76690

Addresses the issue reported in https://github.com/dotnet/sdk-container-builds/issues/192#issuecomment-1269049141 by @rainersigwald

Before this change, it wasn't possible to write into an archive a file entry that contained an unseekable data stream. The undelying cause was that we were calling `Length` to try to get the total number of bytes of the data stream, but it is unsupported when the stream's `CanSeek` is `false`.

The way I fixed this was by separating the code that writes an entry into two possible paths:

- One path for entries with seekable data streams, which remains mostly unmodified.

- A new path for entries with unseekable streams, which changes the order in which we collect the entry information into the buffer:
  - First, write into the buffer all the metadata except for the size field.
  - Then, write the data stream into the archive (this is possible because we know the exact location where the data should start), counting the number of bytes that are written.
  - Afterwards, write that collected length value in the location for the size field in the buffer.
  - Finally, calculate the checksum, then write the buffer into the archive.

issue_context.title: Improve handling when setting an unseekable stream as a tar entry's DataStream
issue_context.body:
Original report here: https://github.com/dotnet/sdk-container-builds/issues/192#issuecomment-1269007374

If the user creates a new regular file tar entry, and sets the `DataStream` to an unseekable stream, we should either:

- Throw immediately if the stream is unseekable in the [TarEntry.cs#L251 setter](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/221717bc1a48f164c5eb2f8ee050f04510a21d41/src/libraries/System.Formats.Tar/src/System/Formats/Tar/TarEntry.cs#L251), or...
- Find a way to retrieve the unseekable stream's length and position without calling Length, right before writing the data to the archive: [TarHeader.Write.cs#L510-L511](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/221717bc1a48f164c5eb2f8ee050f04510a21d41/src/libraries/System.Formats.Tar/src/System/Formats/Tar/TarHeader.Write.cs#L510-L511)

cc @Jozkee

review_comments: Good point. Although I prefer to put it in its own separate debug assert, so that when/if it fails, it's quick and easy to determine exactly which condition failed.

nit: the method name mentions an unseekable stream, while here we get a position of archive stream, so as a person who reads the code I need to check that the dataStream is the unseekable stream. Perhaps the method should be called `WriteFromUnseekableDataStream`? Or `CopyFromUnseekableDataStream`?
I renamed the method to WriteFromUnseekableDataStream as suggested and also added the extra debug assert check to ensure the data stream is unseekable when calling this method.
Good catch because the async version of this method does include the `Data` word in the name.
